reason: I restructured this book eight trading days ago (2026-09-16) on an explicit macro call: a ~5% 10-year Treasury has repriced every low-yield bond-proxy defensive, while a $100+ oil shock pays the energy dividend growers directly. Every leg of that call has strengthened since, so the right action is to let it work rather than pay basis points to re-express a view I already hold. Rates: the 10-year closed 2026-09-28 at ~5.21-5.25%, a 20-year high and still climbing; the Fed hiked 25bp to 3.75-4% on 9/16 in a 12-0 vote with a dot plot signalling one more hike in 2026, against core PCE above 3% every month this year. Oil: Brent settled ~$105.28 on 9/28 after trading as high as $108.83, diesel set a record $6.06/gal on 9/11, and Iran's president publicly refused to back down on 9/23 (oil +4%). This is a military supply shock with no visible diplomatic off-ramp; the 9/28 intraday fade was a Saudi East-West pipeline repair, not a peace deal. Leg-level research confirmed rather than contradicted the book. SCHD (34% core) is +20% YTD versus SPY +13% at a 3.2% forward yield - its 10-year dividend-growth screen is precisely the right filter for this regime. CVX (15%) is +36.9% in 2026, the second-best Dow component, with HSBC raising its target to $250 from $218 on 9/25, RBC reiterating Buy, and the new Venezuela JV set to roughly double production to ~600kbpd; my -2.44% mark is entry timing, having bought eight days after a $217 local high, not thesis damage. MDT (7%) raised FY27 guidance on 9/1 to 7.25-7.75% organic growth on Q1 revenue up 13.7% that beat by $206M, and UBS lifted its target to $110 against an $89.50 mark - the softness is most plausibly arbitrage pressure into the MiniMed exchange-offer expiry on 10/9, a mechanical overhang that clears, so selling now would be selling the discount. EPD (5%) is my worst mark at -3.78% but raised its distribution 2.8% in mid-September on a 28-year growth streak, record Q2 DCF of $2.3B at 1.9x coverage, and guidance for double-digit EBITDA and DCF growth in 2027; a ~7% current yield is short-duration cash flow, exactly what you want to own when the discount rate is 5.25%. ABBV and JNJ are both marking positive and doing their defensive job. The single weakest leg is USB, down from a $65.42 August high to $58.78 with the KBW regional index off 1.5% on hike day, but a 3.75-4% funds rate against a 5.25% ten-year is a steep, NIM-positive curve for one of the best deposit franchises in the country, and I will not pay spread to exit a 5% position on sector beta. Nothing I found broke a thesis. All eight leg P&Ls sit inside +/-4% against stops set at 10-12%, which is noise over eight sessions, and the book's +2.84% NAV trails SPY's +3.26% only marginally while carrying a much shallower -3.44% max drawdown. My risk controls are already correct and live: stops on all eight legs, take-profits on the five names most exposed to an oil reversal or a further rate shock, and 12% cash earning 4% as dry powder if the Iran premium unwinds or the 10-year breaks 5.5%. Churning a confirmed thesis on eight days of noise is how a good book gets traded into a mediocre one.
